seo_description: Pick your first Parfums de Marly by a note you already like: apple and lavender, vanilla and cinnamon, grapefruit, almond or leather. Official notes compared.
summary: A decision guide to five Parfums de Marly fragrances that sends you from a smell you already like to the one to try first, using only the notes on each maker page. It also compares three pairs by their official notes and explains where the house name comes from.

direct_answer: Start with a note you already enjoy. Apple and lavender lead to Layton; cinnamon and orange blossom over vanilla, to Althair; praline with leather, to Haltane; grapefruit and vetiver, to Perseus; almond and anise, to Pegasus. Bergamot sits on all five official note lists, so it cannot decide for you. The order follows those lists and is not a quality ranking.

outline.h2: How do three of these pairs differ on their notes?
points: One sentence of setup: these are the three Parfums de Marly pairings that come up most in search. Do not state search volumes or cite competitor pages.

h3 'Layton vs Pegasus': use head_to_head[0]. Shared notes are only bergamot and vanilla. Layton has apple and cardamom on top, lavender, violet and geranium in the heart, and patchouli, guaiacwood and praline beside the vanilla. Pegasus has anise and almond on top, cypress, violet leaves and orange blossom in the heart, and ambrox and sandalwood beside the vanilla. Optional: the Parfums de Marly site tags Layton 'Fougere Ambery Fruity' and Pegasus 'Fougere Ambery Powdery' on its product cards (quote exactly, cite https://www.parfums-de-marly.com/products/althair, where both cards appear); if used, define fougère from Wikipedia (lavender top notes over oakmoss and coumarin) and do not claim either fragrance contains oakmoss or coumarin.

h3 'Althair vs Layton': use head_to_head[1]. The most shared pair of the five: bergamot, cardamom, vanilla (Althair lists it as bourbon vanilla), guaiacwood and praline. Cardamom sits in Layton's top notes but Althair's heart. Layton alone adds apple, lavender, violet, geranium and patchouli; Althair alone adds mandarin, elemi, orange blossom and cinnamon.

h3 'Haltane vs Althair': use head_to_head[2]. They share only bergamot and praline, and praline sits in Haltane's heart but Althair's base. Haltane adds pink peppercorn, saffron, lavender, clary sage, oud, patchouli, vetiver and leather and lists no vanilla; Althair adds mandarin, elemi, orange blossom, cinnamon, cardamom, bourbon vanilla and guaiacwood.

Each pair ends with one 'Pick by this' sentence phrased as a note preference (for example: if almond appeals more than apple, start with Pegasus). Never phrase it as sweeter, darker, stronger, easier or more versatile.

outline.h2: Where does the Parfums de Marly name come from?
points: Wikipedia describes Parfums de Marly as a French niche perfume house founded in 2009 by Julien Sprecher and headquartered in Paris. Link the live designer vs niche post where the word niche appears.

The name is inspired by the Château de Marly, a residence of King Louis XV (Wikipedia). Wikipedia also says Louis XV was famed for leading the 'perfumed court' and was known for his love of racehorses.

The horse emblem: the house's own story page calls its emblems a tribute to the horses of Marly, 'Masterpieces commissioned in 1743 by Louis XV from the sculptor Guillaume Coustou to adorn the Château entrance.' Use the house page for the 1743 fact (Wikipedia words the 1743 date differently; do not merge the two).

Sprecher's own words, quoted verbatim from the house story page: 'I founded the Maison to express my own vision of modern Haute Parfumerie that disrupts the codes by taking inspiration freely from the spirit of 18th-century France.' Each of the five official product pages states 'All our perfumes are made in France'. Do NOT say each fragrance is named after a particular horse (unsourced), do not name perfumers (not on the pages), and do not reuse post 16's 'What is Parfums de Marly?' sentences or its biography details (birth year, father, Guerlain), which were not fetched this run.

outline.h2: How can you try these five side by side?
points: Compare two at a time, and choose pairs that share notes so the differences are easier to name: Layton with Althair (five shared notes), Layton with Haltane (four), Pegasus with Althair (three). Use one wrist for each and write down which is which.

Smell them at the start and again later the same day, because top, heart and base notes are the groups you notice at different times after spraying (Wikipedia). Say nothing about hours, fading speed or how far a scent reaches.

Keep to one pair per day and write one note-based line about each (for example: 'I kept noticing the almond'). Link the live sample-before-you-buy post on the reason to wear a small amount on real days before buying a bottle.

Use the faq array. Each answer is self-contained (names the fragrance and the house, never says 'as above'), 40 to 90 words, official notes only, no performance language.

picks.h3: 1. Parfums de Marly Layton: for people who like apple with lavender
picks.spelling_note: The house prints 'Guaicwood'. In prose write guaiacwood; in a verbatim quote keep the house spelling.
picks.maker_description_verbatim: Layton blends the freshness of apple with calming lavender, wrapped in the earthy depth of patchouli. Elegant, sensual and flamboyant.
quotable_maker_words: wrapped in the earthy depth of patchouli

table_row.official_notes: Apple, bergamot, cardamom; lavender, violet, geranium; patchouli, vanilla, guaiacwood, praline

picks.wear_it_for: A long Sunday lunch with friends that drifts into the evening.
picks.differs_from_other_four: The only one of the five with apple. It puts cardamom in the top notes (Althair has it in the heart) and is the only list with violet (Pegasus lists violet leaves, a different note). Its base pairs patchouli with vanilla and praline; Haltane has patchouli but no vanilla.
picks.order_reason: Shares 8 of its 10 listed notes with at least one of the other four (bergamot, cardamom, lavender, geranium, patchouli, vanilla, guaiacwood, praline), the most of any, so it is the reference point the chart asks about first. Not a quality ranking.
picks.consistency: Post 26 ranks Layton second and post 51 calls it 'the warm all-rounder'; this article neither ranks it nor reuses that tag. Post 20 (live) lists the same official pyramid. Posts 16, 26 and 34 list jasmine, sandalwood, pepper or top-note lavender, which the current official page does not; use the official list only.

picks.h3: 2. Parfums de Marly Althair: for people who like cinnamon and orange blossom over vanilla
picks.spelling_note: The house spells it Althaïr. Print 'Althair' everywhere (store title and older posts use it) and mention the house spelling once in this h3 block.
picks.maker_description_verbatim: Althaïr combines the smoothness of vanilla, the indulgence of praline, and the brightness of orange blossom. Elegant, generous and charismatic.
quotable_maker_words: the smoothness of vanilla, the indulgence of praline, and the brightness of orange blossom

table_row.if_you_already_like: Cinnamon and orange blossom over vanilla
table_row.official_notes: Bergamot, mandarin, elemi; orange blossom, cinnamon, cardamom; bourbon vanilla, guaiacwood, praline

picks.wear_it_for: The afternoon you finally spend in that bookshop café.
picks.differs_from_other_four: The only one with mandarin, elemi (a resin from the Canarium luzonicum tree) or cinnamon, and the only one whose vanilla is named bourbon vanilla (vanilla named after Île Bourbon, the former name of Réunion). It shares orange blossom with Pegasus and shares guaiacwood and praline in the base with Layton.
picks.order_reason: Shares 6 of its 9 listed notes with the others (bergamot, orange blossom, cardamom, vanilla, guaiacwood, praline), second most, so it is the second question. Not a quality ranking.
picks.consistency: Post 20 (live) uses the same official pyramid and the phrase 'vanilla warmth with a bright floral lift'; do not reuse it or 'glows rather than smothers'. Posts 26, 34 and 42 list passionfruit, heliotrope, tonka bean and white musk, which the current official page does not; do not use them. Do not call it 'the sweetest' (post 26 phrasing and a comparison).

picks.h3: 3. Parfums de Marly Haltane: for people who like praline with leather
picks.maker_description_verbatim: Haltane opens with the aromatic freshness of bergamot and lavender, reveals a subtle gourmand praline heart, then intensifies into the depth of oud. Sophisticated, audacious and powerful.
quotable_maker_words: the aromatic freshness of bergamot and lavender

table_row.official_notes: Bergamot, pink peppercorn; saffron, praline, lavender, clary sage; oud, patchouli, vetiver, leather

picks.wear_it_for: Dinner at the wine bar you have been meaning to try.
picks.differs_from_other_four: The only one with pink peppercorn, saffron, clary sage, oud (agarwood) or leather, and the only one with four heart notes. Its list has no vanilla. Praline sits in its heart, where Layton and Althair list praline in the base. It shares vetiver with Perseus and lavender and patchouli with Layton.
picks.order_reason: Shares 5 of its 10 listed notes with the others (bergamot, praline, lavender, patchouli, vetiver), third most. Low stock: it may appear, but never as the lead or first pick, and this order keeps it third. Not a quality ranking.
picks.consistency: Store notes match the official page. Post 26 calls it 'Sweet and dark at once' and post 42 calls it 'the house's dark one' with smoke; the official page uses neither 'dark' nor 'smoky', so do not use those words. If gourmand is used, define it from Wikipedia (a perfume built mainly on edible notes such as honey, chocolate, vanilla or candy) and quote the maker's 'gourmand praline heart'.

picks.h3: 4. Parfums de Marly Perseus: for people who like grapefruit and vetiver
picks.maker_description_verbatim: Perseus combines bright grapefruit, fresh geranium, and refined vetiver. Bright, invigorating and refined.
quotable_maker_words: bright grapefruit, fresh geranium, and refined vetiver

table_row.official_notes: Bergamot, grapefruit; geranium, blackcurrant bud; vetiver, amberwood, grey amber

picks.wear_it_for: When the plan is a morning walk to the farmers market.
picks.differs_from_other_four: The shortest list of the five, at seven notes. The only one with grapefruit, blackcurrant bud (unopened blackcurrant buds are distilled for a perfumery oil), amberwood or grey amber. Its list has no vanilla, praline or lavender. It shares geranium with Layton and vetiver (a grass whose roots are used in perfume) with Haltane.
picks.order_reason: Shares 3 of its 7 listed notes (bergamot, geranium, vetiver). It ties with Pegasus on shared notes and comes before it because it shares two notes with Haltane, the box before it (bergamot, vetiver), where Pegasus shares one. Not a quality ranking.
picks.consistency: Post 51 calls it 'the bright daily pick' and 'the easiest daily wear'; post 42 tags it for the office; post 26 calls it 'Fresh and polite, the safest PdM'. Reuse none of these and make no office or ease claim. Posts 26 and 42 list green apple, lavender, violet leaf and musk, which the current official page does not. The context lane's family label 'Bright Citrus Woody' was NOT found on any page fetched this run (the product card on the Althair page reads 'Woody Green Citrus'); do not use a family label for Perseus.

picks.h3: 5. Parfums de Marly Pegasus: for people who like almond and anise
picks.maker_description_verbatim: Pegasus opens with radiant bergamot, softened by the smoothness of almond, and unfolds into a warm, captivating vanilla base. Vibrant, addictive and sensual.

table_row.official_notes: Anise, bergamot, almond; cypress, violet leaves, orange blossom; ambrox, vanilla, sandalwood

picks.differs_from_other_four: The only one with anise (a herb with a licorice-like flavour), almond, cypress, violet leaves, ambrox or sandalwood. Its list has no praline and no lavender. It shares orange blossom with Althair and vanilla with Layton and Althair.
picks.order_reason: Shares 3 of its 9 listed notes (bergamot, orange blossom, vanilla), tied with Perseus and placed after it by the tie-break in the Perseus entry. Last in the chart, not last in quality.
picks.consistency: The current official page lists NO lavender, jasmine, heliotrope, bitter almond, amber or guaiac wood. faq.q: Which Parfums de Marly fragrance should I try first?
faq.answer_points: Start from a note you already like: apple and lavender for Layton, cinnamon and orange blossom over vanilla for Althair, praline and leather for Haltane, grapefruit and vetiver for Perseus, almond and anise for Pegasus. All five list bergamot, so it does not help you choose. Say the order is not a quality ranking. 40 to 90 words.

faq.q: Is Layton or Pegasus the better first Parfums de Marly?
faq.answer_points: Neither is better; they share only bergamot and vanilla. Layton lists apple, cardamom, lavender, violet, geranium, patchouli, guaiacwood and praline; Pegasus lists anise, almond, cypress, violet leaves, orange blossom, ambrox and sandalwood. Choose by which of those notes you already enjoy. No comfort, complexity or crowd-pleasing claims.

faq.q: What is the difference between Althair and Layton?
faq.answer_points: They share five listed notes (bergamot, cardamom, vanilla, guaiacwood, praline), more than any other pair of the five. Althair adds mandarin, elemi, orange blossom and cinnamon and names its vanilla bourbon vanilla; Layton adds apple, lavender, violet, geranium and patchouli. Cardamom is a top note in Layton and a heart note in Althair. No sweetness comparison.

faq.q: Which Parfums de Marly fragrances have vanilla in them?
faq.answer_points: Of these five, Layton and Pegasus list vanilla in their base notes and Althair lists bourbon vanilla (define: vanilla named after Île Bourbon, the former name of Réunion). Haltane and Perseus do not list vanilla on their official pages. Layton, Althair and Haltane list praline (define: a confection of nuts, usually almonds, pecans or hazelnuts, and sugar).

faq.q: How is Perseus different from the other Parfums de Marly fragrances here?
faq.answer_points: By its note list: seven notes, the shortest of the five, with no vanilla, praline or lavender. It is the only one with grapefruit, blackcurrant bud, amberwood and grey amber, and it shares geranium with Layton and vetiver with Haltane. Quote the maker's 'bright grapefruit, fresh geranium, and refined vetiver'. No daily, easy, office, safe or season claims.

faq.q: Is Parfums de Marly a niche brand, and where are its perfumes made?
faq.answer_points: Wikipedia describes Parfums de Marly as a French niche perfume house, founded in 2009 by Julien Sprecher and headquartered in Paris. Its official product pages state 'All our perfumes are made in France'. The name comes from the Château de Marly, a residence of Louis XV. Do not define niche beyond linking; no price-tier claims.

A herb with a licorice-like flavour.
A resin harvested from Canarium luzonicum, a tree native to the Philippines.
A perennial bunchgrass that has been used to produce perfumes.
Unopened blackcurrant buds are distilled for an essential oil used in perfumery.
A herb in the sage genus whose distilled oil is used in perfumes.
Wood of the Bulnesia sarmientoi tree, which yields oil of guaiac used in soaps and perfumes.
Agarwood: a fragrant, dark and resinous wood used in incense and perfume.
A spice from the crocus flower with a hay-like fragrance.
Vanilla planifolia, named after Île Bourbon, the former name of Réunion.
A perfume built mainly on edible notes such as honey, chocolate, vanilla or candy.
